cause.classification: model-setting-mismatch
cause.statement: NAIF ITRF93 BPC uses its own EOP/nutation reduction (IAU 1976/1980), whereas the suite supplies daily IERS rows to IAU 2006/2000A. This explains the NAIF-run J2/field offsets. Stock Nyx already uses the FFM-matched BPC, so the NAIF mismatch must not be assigned to stock residuals. Orekit additionally applies subdaily EOP corrections; FFM uses the exported daily rows.

dragSettings.statement: The cached runs predate the runner fix that writes WGS84 into ANISE planetary data. ANISE transform_to replaces supplied frame shape from that data; the old path uses pck08 Earth radii. The current prebuilt published-MSIS runner plus WGS84 brings every supported drag case below 0.1 m. Historical binaries are unavailable, so assignment of the cached residual to that old path is an inference from the documented source fix, file chronology, measured shape difference and corrected-run convergence.

stm.statement: Stock Nyx 2.6.0 spacecraft.rs:208-214 takes ctx.stm (the step-start matrix) and computes stm * grad. grad is the conventional df/dx; the variational equation requires grad * stage_stm. Propagator instance.rs passes the unchanged context to each RK stage. This reversed product and frozen step-start matrix explain the gross disagreements even in point mass; no FFM STM defect is indicated by this comparison.

evidence.source: nyx-space 2.6.0 src/dynamics/spacecraft.rs:199-214; src/propagators/instance.rs:359-394; src/dynamics/orbital.rs:141-155 defines df/dx; spacecraft.rs:330-333 copies that gradient

buildOutputs.note: Historical and current Cargo executable hashes are informational build-output observations, not reproducible identity requirements.

provenance.sourceScope: The pinned runner source is the current documented reproduction recipe, including the WGS84 planetary-data correction used by drag-settings-diagnostic.json. It is not a claim that the unavailable historical executable was built from byte-identical runner source.

diagnosticLock.note: run-nyx.mjs --bin recorded the stock runner Cargo.lock, not the patched runner lock. This is the actual local patched-runner lock. The Nyx crate checksum identifies the unmodified registry crate; the separate patch identifies the two changed formulas.

protocol.units: meters, with STM columns dimensionless relative differences
protocol.frame: GCRF; EME2000 only for E1 cases
protocol.timeScales: UTC sample epochs; FFM integrates TT, Nyx hifitime ET for ephemeris/orientation
protocol.toleranceRationale: Unmodified protocol.tolerancesM.default: point mass 0.001 m, gravity 0.05 m, SRP and drag 0.1 m. The 1.5 m drag allowance belongs only to GMAT and is not applied to Nyx.
protocol.met: The case-level flag uses suite. Each setting also has its own flag; no tolerance is relaxed.
protocol.stm: Largest relative difference of each 6x6 orbit column, position and velocity rows separately; Cr*A/m and Cd*A/m columns use the same definition. No STM pass threshold is specified by the exported protocol, so measured agreement is reported without inventing one.

stockNyx.statement: Stock Nyx 2.6.0 meets tolerance on 54 of 59 cases at the suite setting; the five misses are LEO drag cases affected by the two-line NRLMSISE-00 port defect.

drag.statement: With the published NRLMSISE-00 formulas and the WGS84 Earth shape, the five missed cases are about 0.05 m from FFM, all below the unchanged 0.1 m limit. The exact corrected residuals are recorded per case. The port defect and the cached runner Earth-shape mismatch are separated in the per-case diagnostics; they do not indicate an FFM defect.

stm.statement: The STM comparison is not usable as an FFM check: Nyx uses the step-start ctx.stm and computes stm * grad, instead of grad * stage_stm, while the RK stages retain the same context.
